findings.claim: The tool-free guard rests on --tools "", --permission-mode dontAsk and --setting-sources "". Nothing in the argument list stops claude from loading MCP servers from the user's config or from a candidate-controlled .mcp.json in the worktree. dontAsk with no allow rules should deny those tools, but no test proves it. The package comment itself says the live check of the installed claude is not done. Adding --strict-mcp-config would be cheap defence in depth for a Risk 2 guard.

The adapter builds stdin as instructions plus a blank line plus the brief, then review/app appends the frozen context to the brief. Only the cmd-level test pins the full stdin shape, using a fake runner. A change to the separator in either package would not be caught by the adapter's own test, which uses a brief that has no frozen context.

evidence: ClaudeInstructions rejects each malformed shape the tests list. Its body extraction matches the Codex body in the per-role test.
The runtime switch in review_launch.go keeps the Codex path unchanged. The claude path wires WithFrozenContext and a claude runner whose working directory is the bound worktree.
execrunner.outputIn sets cmd.Dir to the empty string when called from the existing output/OutputStdin, which keeps the previous behaviour for those callers.
